1	# Mise: build spec for a hands-free pantry-to-plate cooking app
2	
3	This SPEC.md specifies **Mise** (working name; rename freely), a Next.js web app built at HackCamp 2026 (nwPlus, UBC Vancouver, Nov 7–8, 2026). Users sign in with **Auth0**, add groceries by barcode, keep a per-user pantry with quantities and expiry dates in **Tiger Data** (TimescaleDB/Postgres), and get **real recipes found online by Gemini**, ranked toward whatever expires soonest. The original recipe is always shown first with attribution; an "AI-adapted" variant appears only when an ingredient is missing. Users cook hands-free with **MediaPipe** webcam gestures (scroll, next/previous step, timer, read aloud), with steps read aloud by **ElevenLabs** and `speechSynthesis` as the fallback. Finishing a recipe deducts what was used from the pantry and logs calories and protein in one database transaction. The app is served over HTTPS from a **Vultr** VPS, which the camera requires. The spec is written so three Claude Code accounts can build it in parallel through **Entire**. A Phase 0 foundation freezes the contracts in `src/contracts/`, the SQL schema and the stubs. After that, three workstreams (Cook Mode, Pantry & Nutrition, Recipes & Cooking Backend) each own separate directories, and an integration phase merges them. Researched facts are cited inline. Anything not confirmed against a primary source in research is marked **[VERIFY]**, and the open items are collected in §17. Treat those as the first things to check, not as settled.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 0. How to use this document
8	
9	- **Who reads this:** three Claude Code agents (one per teammate account) plus the humans steering them. Each agent reads §1–§8 (shared ground truth), its own workstream in §18, and the relevant feature sections in §9.
10	- **Source of truth order:** `src/contracts/**` (code) > this SPEC > comments. If the SPEC and the contracts disagree after Phase 0, the contracts win. Raise the mismatch with a human; don't silently diverge.
11	- **Markers:** **[VERIFY]** = not confirmed against a primary source during research; check before relying on it. **P0** = required for the demo, **P1** = should have, **P2** = stretch.
12	- Anthropic's guidance for specs like this: "The most useful specs are self-contained: they name the files and interfaces involved, state what is out of scope, and end with an end-to-end verification step." Keep CLAUDE.md short ([Claude Code best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md)). This spec follows both.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Overview, goals and non-goals
17	
18	### 1.1 Problem and pitch
19	
20	Home cooks waste food they forgot they had, and following a recipe on a phone or laptop with wet, floury hands is awkward. Screens dim and you lose your place. Mise closes the loop: **scan groceries → know what expires → cook a real recipe that uses it → touch nothing while cooking → pantry and nutrition update themselves.** HackCamp's challenge is to "identify a problem facing a community and build a solution that makes a meaningful difference". Judging covers Problem & User Research, Innovation, Technical Implementation, Design & UX, and Presentation ([HackCamp 2026 Devpost](https://hackcamp-2026.devpost.com/)).
21	
22	### 1.2 Goals (all confirmed by the team)
23	
24	| # | Goal | Priority |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| G1 | Web app: Next.js App Router + TypeScript, deployed on Vultr over HTTPS | P0 |
27	| G2 | Auth0 login. Every pantry item, recipe, session and meal belongs to one user | P0 |
28	| G3 | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB/Postgres) as the only database | P0 |
29	| G4 | Add groceries by barcode, scanned with the camera or typed. Lookup chain: **dataandapis.com → Open Food Facts → Gemini reads a product/label photo → manual form** | P0 |
30	| G5 | Expiry date from a photo of the printed date (Gemini reads it, user confirms) or typed in | P0 |
31	| G6 | Pantry tracks quantities and expiry dates, and deducts ingredients after cooking | P0 |
32	| G7 | Gemini finds **real recipes online**, shown **original-first with source attribution**, ranked to prefer items closest to expiry | P0 |
33	| G8 | Only when an ingredient is missing, AI may propose an adaptation, clearly marked **"AI-adapted"** and kept separate from the original | P0 |
34	| G9 | MediaPipe hand gestures: scroll up/down, next/previous step, start/pause step timer, read step aloud | P0 |
35	| G10 | Read aloud with ElevenLabs, falling back to browser `speechSynthesis` | P0 |
36	| G11 | Nutrition per pantry item and per recipe serving. Strict, code-enforced diet/allergy filters. Daily calorie and protein tracking | P0 |
37	| G12 | Meals logged through a "Finish cooking" prompt (servings eaten) and through manual logging | P0 |
38	| G13 | Built by 3 Claude Code accounts collaborating through Entire (Sessions, Graph, Brain, Trails) | P0 |
39	
40	### 1.3 Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)
41	
42	- Native mobile apps. PWA install/offline mode is also out (the site should still work in mobile browsers).
43	- Writing recipes from scratch with AI. The AI only *finds* recipes and *adapts* them when ingredients are missing.
44	- Medical or dietetic advice, or certified allergen guarantees. The app filters strictly but tells users to check labels.
45	- Shopping lists, grocery ordering, price tracking, meal planning calendars.
46	- Sharing pantries between users or households, and any social features.
47	- Contributing products back to Open Food Facts, which would need an OFF account for writes ([OFF API intro](https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/)).
48	- Voice *commands* (speech recognition) are P2 only. The P0 hands-free channel is gestures plus read-aloud.
49	- Moving gesture inference to a Web Worker (P2; see §11.7).
50	- Hosted vector search or "similar recipes" (P2).
51	
52	### 1.4 Glossary
53	
54	- **Original recipe:** the recipe exactly as parsed from the publisher's page (schema.org `Recipe`), with attribution. Never modified.
55	- **AI-adapted recipe:** a separate object that references an original and lists explicit substitutions for missing ingredients.
56	- **Base units:** grams (mass), millilitres (volume), `count` (pieces). Every stored quantity uses one of them.
57	- **GTIN:** the canonical 13-digit (or 14-digit) barcode key. UPC-A is left-padded with `0`.
58	- **FEFO:** first-expired-first-out, the rule for choosing which pantry row to deduct from.
59	- **Armed:** the gesture state in which commands are accepted. Users arm it by holding an open palm.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 2. User flows
64	
65	Each flow lists its happy path, then its branches. Feature IDs (F#) refer to §9.
66	
67	### UF1: Sign in and onboarding (F1)
68	1. A visitor lands on `/`. The marketing hero has a "Sign in" button that links to `/auth/login` (Auth0 Universal Login).
69	2. After callback, the first authenticated request upserts a `users` row keyed by Auth0 `sub`.
70	3. If `onboarded_at` is null, redirect to `/onboarding`. There the user sets diets (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, high-protein), allergens, daily kcal and protein goals (optional), and time zone (default `America/Vancouver`).
71	4. The user lands on `/today`.
72	
73	### UF2: Add a grocery by barcode (F2, F4, F5)
74	1. `/pantry/add` opens the camera scanner, with the **"Type barcode" input always visible**.
75	2. A code is accepted after 2 identical consecutive reads and a valid check digit. The client calls `POST /api/products/lookup`.
76	3. **Found** (cache, dataandapis or OFF): show a confirmation card with name, brand, image, nutrition per 100 g, package size, and source attribution ("Data: Open Food Facts, ODbL").
77	4. The user sets quantity (pre-filled from package size when known) and unit, then sets expiry: **"Photo of date"** (UF4) or **"Enter date"** or "No date".
78	5. Save. The item appears in `/pantry`, sorted by soonest expiry.
79	- **Branch, not found:** "We couldn't find this product." → **"Take photo of product & nutrition label"** (UF3) → if that fails or is declined → **manual form**. The manual form is reachable from every step.
80	- **Branch, provider down** (401/402/429/5xx/timeout): treated as a miss for the user, logged server-side. The flow continues to OFF, then to the photo step.
81	
82	### UF3: Product from a label photo (F3)
83	1. The user captures 1–3 photos (front, nutrition panel, optional side). The client downscales them to about 1600 px on the long edge, JPEG q≈0.85.
84	2. `POST /api/vision/label` → Gemini returns a draft and the server runs sanity checks.
85	3. The manual form opens **pre-filled**. Flagged fields are highlighted. The user must press **Confirm** before anything is saved (`userVerified=true`).
86	
87	### UF4: Expiry date from a photo (F4)
88	1. The user takes a close photo of the printed date.
89	2. `POST /api/vision/expiry` → the server assembles a date from Gemini's components and cross-checks it with a CFIA regex.
90	3. A date picker opens pre-filled, with the raw text shown ("Read: `BB/MA 2026 NO 15`"). If the order is ambiguous, the user picks from the candidates. **The user must confirm.** "Packaged on" dates are never accepted as expiry; instead the UI says "This looks like a packaged-on date".
91	
92	### UF5: Find recipes (F6, F7, F10)
93	1. `/recipes` shows chips for expiring-soon items (≤ 3 days, pre-selected) and a "Find recipes" button. The user's diet/allergy filters appear as locked chips with a link to Settings.
94	2. `POST /api/recipes/search` streams progress ("Searching the web… / Reading 8 recipe pages… / Checking your allergies…"), then candidate cards arrive one by one.
95	3. Each card shows the title, the **source site and author**, coverage ("You have 7 of 9 ingredients"), the expiring items it uses (badge "uses spinach, expires in 2 days"), missing-ingredient count, ≈kcal and protein per serving, and total time.
96	4. Candidates that break a diet or allergy filter never appear. A collapsed "N recipes hidden by your filters" note lists them by reason (no recipe content shown).
97	
98	### UF6: Recipe detail, original first, optional adaptation (F8, F9, F10)
99	1. `/recipes/[recipeId]` shows the **Original** card first: title, "From {siteName} by {author}", a "View original" link, ingredients exactly as published (each marked have / missing / staple), steps, and nutrition (our estimate with coverage, plus "Publisher's nutrition" if the page provided it).
100	2. If the recipe has missing ingredients, a secondary button reads **"Suggest an AI adaptation using my pantry"**. Pressing it calls `POST /api/recipes/[id]/adapt`. The result appears in a **separate card with an "AI-adapted" badge** on a different background. It lists substitutions ("Missing: buttermilk → Using: Greek yogurt + lemon (from your pantry)"), changed steps, warnings, and re-estimated nutrition.
101	3. "Cook original" and "Cook AI-adapted" (when present) are separate buttons, each with a servings stepper.
102	
103	### UF7: Cook hands-free (F11, F12, F13)
104	1. "Cook" → `POST /api/cook/sessions` → `/cook/[sessionId]`. The **"Start cooking" tap** unlocks audio and requests a screen wake lock.
105	2. One step per screen, in large type. The step's ingredients and quantities are listed and timer chips are docked at the bottom.
106	3. A **"Hands-free" toggle** loads MediaPipe lazily, asks for camera permission, and shows the HUD with a gesture legend. Open palm (hold) arms the system. Then swipe = next/previous, thumb up/down (hold) = scroll, fist (hold) = timer start/pause, victory sign (hold) = read step aloud / stop.
107	4. Each control also has big tap targets and keyboard shortcuts.
108	5. Refreshing or reopening the page offers "Resume at step 5?". Timers continue correctly because they are stored as absolute end times.
109	
110	### UF8: Finish cooking (F14)
111	1. On the last step (or any time from the menu) → **"Finish cooking"** dialog.
112	2. The dialog shows **Servings cooked** (default = planned), **Servings you ate** (default 1; 0 allowed), and a **deduction preview** with one line per matched pantry item ("Spinach: 150 g of 200 g → 50 g left"). Lines are editable and can be unchecked. Lines the app couldn't convert are flagged "Adjust manually". The nutrition for the servings eaten is editable.
113	3. Confirm → one transaction deducts the pantry, writes pantry events, inserts the meal log and closes the session → navigate to `/today` with a toast ("Logged 1 serving · 540 kcal · 32 g protein").
114	
115	### UF9: Daily tracking and manual logging (F15)
116	1. `/today` shows kcal and protein rings against the goals, today's meals list, a 7-day bar chart, and "Expiring soon" pantry items.
117	2. **"Log food"** offers three tabs: *From pantry* (pick item + amount; "Also remove from pantry" checkbox, default on), *Scan* (barcode → product → amount), *Quick add* (label + kcal + protein).
118	3. The user can delete a meal from today's list.
119	
120	---
121

123	
124	### 3.1 System diagram
125

256	### 5.1 Design rules
257	
258	- **Base units everywhere.** Store `quantity_base` in g, ml or count, and keep the user's `display_unit` alongside for display.
259	- **Nutrition per 100 g or 100 ml** is canonical. Per serving is derived, or stored when the source gives it.
260	- **Mutable state goes in plain tables:** `pantry_items`, `recipes`, `recipe_variants`, `cooking_sessions`.

1252	### F11. Cooking mode UI (P0), owned by A
1253	
1254	**Requirements.** `/cook/[sessionId]`, client-heavy, built on `CookSessionView`. All inputs (touch, keyboard, gestures, optional voice) go through one `CookingController` backed by a `useReducer` state machine: `{ stepIndex, timers: StepTimer[], speaking, scrollY }`.
1255	- **Layout:** one step per screen. Step text ≥ 32 px (40 px on screens ≥ 1024 px wide). "Step 4 of 12" plus a progress bar. The step's ingredients with scaled quantities. Timer chips docked at the bottom. Prev and Next tap zones each ≥ 25% of the screen width. High contrast, dark theme by default. (Sizes are design heuristics, not sourced.)
1256	- **Wake lock:** request `navigator.wakeLock.request("screen")` in the "Start cooking" click, re-acquire it on `visibilitychange` → visible, and release it on finish, exit, or 30 min of inactivity. If `!("wakeLock" in navigator)`, hide the "Screen stays on" indicator rather than showing a broken control. The API is Baseline 2025, needs HTTPS, and can be rejected in power-save mode ([MDN Screen Wake Lock](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Screen_Wake_Lock_API)). Keeping the screen on is proven to matter: Betty Crocker saw 3.1× longer sessions and 50% lower bounce ([web.dev case study](https://web.dev/case-studies/betty-crocker)).
1257	- **Timers:**
1258	  - Parse durations from step text with `/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?:\s*(?:-|–|to)\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?))?\s*(seconds?|secs?|minutes?|mins?|hours?|hrs?)\b/i`. Use the **lower bound** of a range, so the cook checks early. Sum compound durations ("1 hour 15 minutes").
1259	  - Steps without a duration get a **stopwatch** (count-up) when toggled.
1260	  - Store timers as absolute `endsAt`/`startedAt` epoch ms. Remaining time is always `endsAt − Date.now()` and never a decrementing counter. Chrome throttles hidden-tab timers to once per minute after 5 minutes ([Chrome timer throttling](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/timer-throttling-in-chrome-88)).
1261	  - Multiple concurrent timers are allowed, each labelled with its step.
1262	  - Alarm: Web Audio beep plus `navigator.vibrate` plus a `Notification` if permission was granted. On `visibilitychange` → visible, check immediately for elapsed timers.
1263	- **Recovery:** persist `{sessionId, stepIndex, timers, updatedAt}` to `localStorage` on every change. On load, if the state is less than 12 h old, offer "Resume at step N?". `PATCH /api/cook/sessions/:id {currentStep}` is debounced to 2 s.
1264	- **Keyboard:** ←/→ steps, ↑/↓ and PgUp/PgDn scroll, **T** or **Space** toggles the timer, **R** reads aloud or stops, **Esc** exits hands-free.
1265	- **Announcements:** an `aria-live="polite"` region announces step changes and fired actions. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
1266	- **Finish:** a "Finish cooking" button on the last step and in the menu opens `FinishDialog` (F14).
1267	
1268	**AC**
1269	1. Pressing → advances the step, announces "Step 5 of 12" in the live region, and stops any speech in progress.
1270	2. Start a 10-minute timer, reload the page, accept "Resume". The timer shows the correct remaining time (±1 s).
1271	3. Hide the tab for 2 minutes with a 1-minute timer running. On return, the alarm fires immediately.
1272	4. Wake lock is held during cooking (`wakeLock.released === false`) and released after Finish.
1273	5. "Simmer for 10–15 minutes" yields a 10:00 countdown. "Season to taste" yields a stopwatch when toggled.

1310	### F14. Finish cooking: pantry deduction and meal log (P0), owned by C (server) and A (dialog UI)
1311	
1312	**Requirements.**
1313	- `GET finish-preview` plans deductions (`server/cook/plan.ts`). For each matched ingredient line:
1314	
1315	  `needBase = qtyBase × servingsCooked / variant.servings`
1316	
1317	  Then convert to the pantry item's dim (bridge or `unconvertible`), choose the pantry row by explicit `pantryItemId` from matching (substitutions use their `pantryItemId`) or by FEFO, and clamp at the available quantity (`clamped`).
1318	- The dialog lets the user edit quantities, uncheck lines, set servings cooked and eaten, and edit kcal and protein per serving.
1319	- `POST finish` runs **one transaction** (`server/cook/finish.ts`), following the research notes' design:
1320	  1. `UPDATE cooking_sessions SET status='finished', finished_at=now(), servings_cooked, servings_eaten WHERE id AND user_id AND status='in_progress' RETURNING …`. If no row, throw 409. This is the idempotency guard.
1321	  2. For each confirmed deduction: `SELECT quantity_base … FOR UPDATE` scoped by `user_id`, `take = min(available, requested)`, update the quantity (never below 0), and insert `pantry_events(kind='cook_deduct', delta_base=-take, cooking_session_id)`.
1322	  3. If `servingsEaten > 0`: insert `meal_logs(source='cooking_session', label=title, servings=servingsEaten, kcal = perServing.kcal × servingsEaten, protein_g = …, local_date = today in users.tz)`.
1323	- **Decisions:**
1324	  - Clamp at 0 and don't fail.
1325	  - Keep rows at 0 for "Restock".
1326	  - `servings_cooked` drives deduction and `servings_eaten` drives calories; they differ when there are leftovers.
1327	  - Meal nutrition is a snapshot.
1328	
1329	**AC**
1330	1. Finishing with 200 g spinach in the pantry and 150 g needed leaves 50 g, adds a `pantry_events` row of −150, and adds a `meal_logs` row with `source='cooking_session'`.
1331	2. Posting finish twice: the second call returns 409, and the pantry is deducted only once.
1332	3. `servingsEaten=0` deducts the pantry and creates no meal log.
1333	4. An ingredient in cups matched to a pantry item in grams with no density shows `unconvertible` in the preview and is not deducted.
1334	5. If any statement fails (simulate by deleting the pantry row mid-request), nothing is written.

1535	### 10.5 ElevenLabs text-to-speech
1536	
1537	- **Request:** `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream?output_format=mp3_44100_128`
1538	  - Header `xi-api-key`.
1539	  - Body `{ text, model_id: "eleven_flash_v2_5" }`. The API default model is `eleven_multilingual_v2`, so **always set the model explicitly**.
1540	  - `optimize_streaming_latency` is deprecated.
1541	  - Source: [Stream speech](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/stream)
1542	- **Why HTTP streaming:** it is the recommended mode "for cases where the input text is available up-front", which fits recipe steps. WebSockets are for incremental LLM text ([latency guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/best-practices/latency-optimization.md)).
1543	- **Model choice:** Flash v2.5 has about 100 ms median model latency, up to 40,000 characters per request, 32 languages, and 50% lower per-character price. `eleven_turbo_v2_5` is deprecated ([Models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models)).
1544	- **Cost:** Flash/Turbo API pricing is **$0.04 per 1K characters** ([API pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api)). A 15-step recipe at about 150 characters per step comes to roughly $0.09, and caching makes repeat demos close to free.
1545	- **Route** (`app/api/tts/route.ts`):
1546	  1. Validate 1–2000 chars.
1547	  2. If there is no key, return 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`.
1548	  3. Stream `r.body` through with `Content-Type: audio/mpeg` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`.
1549	  4. If the upstream response is non-2xx, return 502, and the client falls back.

1551	### 10.6 MediaPipe Tasks Vision
1552	
1553	- **Package and assets:** `@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.2.2`. It ships two WASM variants of about 14.6 MB each, and types `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(basePath?, useModule?)`, `BaseOptions.delegate: "CPU" | "GPU"` and `recognizeForVideo(frame, timestamp)`, which is synchronous ([npm tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision)).
1554	- **Model file:** the canonical model URL is `https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/gesture_recognizer/gesture_recognizer/float16/latest/gesture_recognizer.task` ([overview](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer)). Download it once, commit it to `public/models/`, and **[VERIFY]** that the URL serves (research couldn't reach it through the sandbox proxy).
1555	- **Self-hosting:** `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` (postinstall) copies `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/wasm/*` → `public/mediapipe/wasm/`. Never use the `@latest` CDN path. The package shipped four minor releases in Oct–Nov 2026.
1556	- **Canned gestures:** None, Closed_Fist, Open_Palm, Pointing_Up, Thumb_Down, Thumb_Up, Victory, ILoveYou. **Handedness is reported for the subject's hand, and a mirrored image inverts it** ([overview](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer)).
1557	- **Threading:** `recognizeForVideo()` blocks the UI thread, and Google recommends web workers for camera input ([web guide](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer/web_js)). We start on the main thread behind `GestureSource` (§11.7).
1558	- **Performance:** the only published benchmarks are for a Pixel 6: GestureRecognizer averages about 16.8 ms on CPU and 20.9 ms on GPU. Laptop numbers are unknown, so ship a dev FPS counter.

1582	## 11. Gesture state machine (owned by A)
1583	
1584	No published thresholds exist for kitchen gesture control. Every number below is an **engineering starting value to tune**, exposed in `GestureConfig` and adjustable in Settings ("Sensitivity", "Hold time", "Swipe direction", "Always armed").
1585	
1586	### 11.1 Mapping
1587	
1588	| User control (confirmed) | Gesture | Fires | Why |
1589	|---|---|---|---|
1590	| *(prerequisite)* Arm | `Open_Palm` held ≥ **600 ms** | `ARM`, armed for **5 s**. The window extends after each action | Stirring, chopping and reaching never fire commands |
1591	| Next / previous step | **Horizontal swipe** while armed | `NEXT_STEP` / `PREV_STEP` | Natural page turn. Default: hand moves **right→left = next** (phone-carousel convention), configurable |
1592	| Scroll up / down | `Thumb_Up` / `Thumb_Down` held | First tick at **600 ms**, then every **700 ms** while held, each scrolling **40% of the viewport** | Avoids up/down swipes, which collide with stirring and reaching |
1593	| Start / pause step timer | `Closed_Fist` held ≥ **800 ms**, score ≥ **0.8** | `TIMER_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Distinct pose. A long hold and high score guard against a fist around a spoon handle |
1594	| Read step aloud / stop | `Victory` held ≥ **800 ms** | `SPEAK_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Rare in kitchen motion and easier to form than ILoveYou |
1595	
1596	Recognizer options:
1597	- `runningMode: 'VIDEO'`, `numHands: 1`.
1598	- `cannedGesturesClassifierOptions: { scoreThreshold: 0.6, categoryAllowlist: ['Open_Palm','Closed_Fist','Thumb_Up','Thumb_Down','Victory'] }`. The option comes from the [1.2.2 types](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision).
1599	- The engine applies `minScore = 0.7` (and 0.8 for the fist).
1600	
1601	### 11.2 States and transitions
1602	
1603	```
1604	 off ──toggle on──► loading ──model+camera ok──► no_hand
1605	  ▲                   │ └─permission denied──► permission_needed ──retry──► loading
1606	  │                   └─model/wasm fail──► error (buttons/keyboard still work)
1607	  └─toggle off / page hide / route leave (stop tracks, close recognizer)
1608	
1609	 no_hand ──hand detected (bbox h ≥ 8% frame, not touching edge)──► hand_seen
1610	 hand_seen ──no hand ≥ 300 ms──► no_hand
1611	 hand_seen ──Open_Palm held ≥ armHoldMs──► armed   (emit ARM; armedUntil = now + 5000)
1612	 armed ──pose P ∈ {Closed_Fist, Victory, Thumb_Up, Thumb_Down} starts──► holding(P)
1613	 holding(P) ──P held ≥ threshold──► emit action ──► cooldown   (scroll: repeat tick, stays holding)
1614	 holding(P) ──P changes / hand lost before threshold──► armed
1615	 armed ──swipe detected──► emit NEXT/PREV ──► cooldown
1616	 cooldown ──cooldownMs elapsed AND released (pose changed or no hand ≥ 300 ms)──► armed
1617	 armed ──now > armedUntil──► hand_seen / no_hand   (emit DISARM)
1618	 any ──alwaysArmed=true──► arming step skipped
1619	```
1620	
1621	Rules:
1622	- **Release-to-rearm:** a discrete pose action fires at most once per continuous hold.
1623	- **Global cooldown:** 1200 ms after any discrete action (swipe, timer, speak). Scroll ticks don't trigger it, but a release after scrolling adds a 300 ms cooldown.
1624	- **Successful actions extend the armed window** by another 5 s from the action time.
1625	
1626	### 11.3 Swipe detection
1627	
1628	- Palm centre = mean of landmarks **0, 5, 9, 13, 17**. Smooth with an EMA (α = 0.5) before computing velocity.
1629	- Mirror x so directions match what the user sees: `x' = 1 − x`. **Never use the handedness label for direction.**
1630	- Keep a ring buffer of `{t, x, y}` over the last **400 ms**.
1631	- Fire when **all** of these hold:
1632	  - `|Δx| ≥ 0.25` of frame width
1633	  - `|Δx| ≥ 2·|Δy|`
1634	  - peak velocity ≥ **1.0 frame-widths/s**
1635	  - the pose was not `Closed_Fist` for most of the window
1636	- After firing, clear the buffer. The 1200 ms cooldown also swallows the return stroke.
1637	
1638	### 11.4 Constants (`features/gesture/config.ts`)
1639	
1640	```ts
1641	export const DEFAULT_GESTURE_CONFIG: GestureConfig = {
1642	  minScore: 0.7, fistMinScore: 0.8, classifierScoreThreshold: 0.6,
1643	  armHoldMs: 600, actionHoldMs: 800, armWindowMs: 5000, alwaysArmed: false,
1644	  cooldownMs: 1200, releaseMs: 300,
1645	  scrollFirstMs: 600, scrollRepeatMs: 700, scrollFraction: 0.4,
1646	  swipeWindowMs: 400, swipeMinDx: 0.25, swipeDxToDyRatio: 2, swipeMinVelocity: 1.0,
1647	  swipeNextDirection: 'left',
1648	  minHandHeightFrac: 0.08, targetFps: 15, idleFps: 5, idleAfterMs: 10_000,
1649	  delegate: 'GPU',
1650	};
1651	```
1652	
1653	### 11.5 Runtime loop (main thread, `features/gesture/MediaPipeGestureSource.ts`)
1654	
1655	- **Loading:** `GestureController` is a `'use client'` component loaded with `next/dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` from **another client component**. `ssr:false` is not supported in Server Components ([Next.js lazy loading](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/lazy-loading)).
1656	- **Init:** `forVisionTasks('/mediapipe/wasm')`, then `GestureRecognizer.createFromOptions(...)` with `delegate: 'GPU'`, catching failure and retrying with `'CPU'`. Make the delegate configurable, because GPU was *slower* than CPU on the Pixel 6 benchmark.
1657	- **Camera:** `getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: 'user', width: {ideal: 640}, height: {ideal: 480}, frameRate: {ideal: 30} }, audio: false })`. Map `NotAllowedError`, `NotFoundError` and `NotReadableError`, and handle `navigator.mediaDevices === undefined` (insecure context). A prompt the user ignores may never settle, so show "Waiting for camera permission…" ([MDN getUserMedia](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia)).
1658	- **Frame loop:** a rAF loop that processes a frame only when `video.readyState >= 2 && video.currentTime !== last`, throttled to `targetFps`. Drop to `idleFps` after `idleAfterMs` with no hand. Pass a monotonic `performance.now()` timestamp ([HandLandmarker web guide](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/hand_landmarker/web_js)).
1659	- **Strict Mode:** React runs an extra setup and cleanup cycle in dev ([React StrictMode](https://react.dev/reference/react/StrictMode)), so use an `aborted` flag and full cleanup: `cancelAnimationFrame`, stop the tracks, `recognizer.close()`.
1660	- **Visibility:** pause on `visibilitychange` (hidden).
1661	- **State placement:** keep the recognizer, stream and engine in refs. Push HUD state to React at ≤ 10 Hz.
1662	
1663	### 11.6 HUD
1664	
1665	- **Placement:** a corner widget, ≤ 20% of the screen.
1666	- **Contents:**
1667	  - Optional mirrored camera thumbnail (toggle; off hides the video element but keeps inference running).
1668	  - State chip: "Show your palm to start" → "Ready · 4 s" → "Hold fist… ◔" → "Timer started ✓".
1669	  - Radial hold-progress ring.
1670	  - Gesture legend (5 icons).
1671	  - Hints: "Move closer" (hand bbox < 8%), "Turn on a light" (low confidence for 3 s), "One hand please".
1672	- **Debug:** landmarks are drawn only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_GESTURE_DEBUG=true`.
1673	- **Feedback:** every fired action produces a brief full-screen edge flash plus a soft click sound (respecting reduced motion) and an `aria-live` announcement, because the cook is often looking at the pan rather than the screen.
1674	- **Camera indicator:** a persistent "Camera on" pill with a one-tap off switch.
1675	
1676	### 11.7 Worker offload (P2)
1677	
1678	The `GestureSource` interface allows a `WorkerGestureSource`:
1679	- The main thread posts transferable `VideoFrame`/`ImageBitmap` objects, with one frame in flight.
1680	- The worker is created with `new Worker(new URL('./gesture.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` and initialized with `forVisionTasks(base, true)`.
1681	- Fishjam used this pattern in production ([Fishjam blog](https://fishjam.swmansion.com/blog/real-time-gesture-recognition-in-videoconferencing-4711855a1a53)).
1682	- Module workers have a history of `importScripts` breakage, and a maintainer said 0.10.35 "should work" ([issue #5257](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe/issues/5257)). `DrawingUtils` fails in workers. Test on Safari before switching.
1683	
1684	### 11.8 Testability
1685	
1686	- `GestureEngine` is a pure class: `update(result: GestureRecognizerResult-like, now: number)`. It takes no DOM or MediaPipe imports, so Vitest can drive it with synthetic landmark sequences in `features/gesture/__fixtures__/`.
1687	- `KeyboardGestureSource` (Phase 0 mock) maps keys to `GestureAction`s so Cook Mode can be built before MediaPipe works.

1691	## 12. UX rules (apply everywhere)
1692	
1693	1. **Original before AI, always.** Anything Gemini *generated or transformed* carries a visible badge: "AI-adapted" on adaptations, "Read by AI, please confirm" on label and expiry drafts, "≈ estimate" on computed nutrition. Publisher content carries attribution instead.
1694	2. **Confirm before save** for every AI extraction. Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap.
1695	3. **Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent.** Gestures are never the only path, and hands-free is opt-in per session.
1696	4. **Kitchen-distance readability in cook mode:**
1697	   - Step text ≥ 32 px.
1698	   - One step per screen.
1699	   - Tap targets ≥ 25% of width for Prev and Next, and ≥ 56 px elsewhere.
1700	   - Contrast ≥ WCAG AA. Dark theme default in cook mode.
1701	5. **Colour is never the only signal.** Expiry bands also show text ("2 days"), and have/missing markers use icon + label.
1702	6. **Feedback for hands-free actions** goes through three channels: visual flash, sound, and `aria-live` text. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
1703	7. **Progressive results.** Recipe search streams status messages and cards. Never show a spinner with no message for more than 2 s.
1704	8. **Honest empty and error states:**
1705	   - "We couldn't find this product" leads straight to the next fallback.
1706	   - "Camera blocked" offers buttons and keyboard.
1707	   - "Voice: Device" appears when ElevenLabs is unavailable.
1708	9. **"Best before", not "Expires"**, unless Gemini classified the date as `expiry`/`use_by`. Show the raw printed text next to the parsed date.
1709	10. **Allergy copy:** filters are strict, but the app always says "Always check product labels for allergens." Never claim a recipe is "safe".
1710	11. **Units:** show the user's display unit and accept common abbreviations. Never show raw base units to users.
1711	12. **Design deliverable:** produce a Figma file of the main screens (Today, Pantry, Scan, Recipes, Recipe detail with Original + AI-adapted, Cook mode + HUD) for the Best Design submission (§16).

1715	## 13. Security and privacy
1716	
1717	| Area | Rule |
1718	|---|---|
1719	| Secrets | Server-only. None use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix. `.env.production` lives on the VPS with `chmod 600` and is never baked into the image. Entire's secrets redaction is a bonus, not a control |
1720	| AuthZ | `requireUser()` in every route handler and Server Action. Every SQL statement includes `user_id = ${user.id}`. IDs in URLs are always re-checked against the user, and a mismatch returns **404** (not 403) |
1721	| Input validation | Zod on every body and query. Barcode digits 8–14. Text caps (TTS 2000, freeText 100). Image MIME allowlist and ≤ 4 MB each, ≤ 3 per request |
1722	| LLM output | Treated as untrusted input: Zod-validated, values sanity-checked, pantry IDs verified, allergens re-checked in code, URLs verified by fetch |
1723	| SSRF (recipe fetcher) | `server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts`: only `http(s)` on ports 80/443. Resolve DNS and **reject private, loopback, link-local and metadata IPs** (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7), re-checked on every redirect. Max 5 redirects, 5 s timeout, 2 MB body cap, `text/html` only |
1724	| Rendering third-party HTML | Never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` publisher HTML. Parse it to text. Gemini's Search Suggestions HTML is rendered **unmodified inside a sandboxed `<iframe srcdoc>`** (`sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"`) **[VERIFY this satisfies the Grounding display terms]** |
1725	| Camera and video | Frames are processed locally and never recorded, uploaded or stored. Model and WASM are self-hosted, so there are no third-party requests while hands-free is on. The camera starts only after an explicit toggle, a persistent indicator is shown, and tracks stop on toggle-off, page hide and route leave |
1726	| Photos | Label and expiry photos go to Gemini through our server for one request and are **not persisted** (memory only). The UI copy says so |
1727	| Headers | `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=()`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`. CSP (P1): `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`; `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:`; `media-src 'self' blob:`; `connect-src 'self'`; `worker-src 'self' blob:`. The `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` source is needed for Emscripten WASM (general knowledge **[VERIFY]**) |
1728	| Abuse and cost | Per-user rate limits (§7). TTS text cap. Discovery cache. Barcode cache and single-flight |
1729	| Licensing and attribution | "Product data © Open Food Facts contributors, ODbL" in the footer and on product cards. OFF images are CC BY-SA. Recipe attribution and "View original" on every recipe |
1730	| Data deletion | Settings → "Delete my data" deletes the `users` row (cascades) (P1) |

2082	## Conclusion
2083	
2084	The riskiest parts of this build aren't gestures or auth. They are three LLM boundaries: finding real URLs, reading labels and dates, and adapting recipes. In each one, Gemini's output can be well-formed and still wrong. The spec therefore keeps Gemini out of every decision that has to be correct. Gemini finds candidate URLs, but the recipe content shown is whatever the publisher's own markup says, fetched and parsed by our code. Gemini reads a label, but a person confirms it. Gemini proposes a substitution, and `checkDiet` decides whether it is allowed. That split is also what lets three agents work in parallel safely, because the deterministic modules (units, GTIN, diet, scoring, timers, the gesture engine) are pure and testable against frozen contracts with no network. The two choices most worth revisiting after the event are the gesture thresholds in §11.4, which no published study validates, and how much publisher step text to store. That second one is a product and legal call, and the research could only partly settle it.

The spec assumes classic dynamic rendering. Keep it or turn it off?

The speaking indicator and SPEAK_TOGGLE logic now see 'not speaking' while step 2 is audible, so the next toggle starts the step again instead of stopping it. Fix: have each utterance's handler check that it is still the current utterance (`if (u === current) set(false)`).

Request changes: on Android Chrome the timer alarm can throw while ringing, and step progress can be lost on exit.

- [high] `src/features/cook/alarm.ts:29`: `new Notification("Timer done", …)` throws `TypeError: Illegal constructor` on Android Chrome. That browser only allows notifications through `ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification`. If the user has granted permission, the first timer to finish throws inside the `state.fired` effect (`CookView.tsx:119-122`). The loop stops, so other timers that finish on the same tick never ring, and the screen-reader message is never set. The error also escapes into React's error handling, which can take down the cook view. A phone is the main device for cooking. Fix: wrap the call in try/catch, or use `navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then(r => r.showNotification(...))` when it is available.
- [medium] `src/features/cook/CookView.tsx:95-98`: The `currentStep` save to the server waits 2 s, and the effect cleanup cancels the pending timeout. Pressing Exit (`router.push` unmounts the view), closing the tab, or leaving within 2 s of the last Next/Prev therefore never sends that step. On another device, or after the 12 h local copy expires, resume offers an older step. Fix: in the cleanup and in `exit()`, send the pending step right away (for example with `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })`) instead of dropping it.
- [low] `src/features/cook/CookView.tsx:296`: `now` only updates while a timer runs. It holds the time of page load or of the last tick, so for up to 500 ms after a timer starts the display uses a stale `now`. A countdown shows extra time, for example 15:00 for a 10-minute timer started 5 minutes after load. A stopwatch gets a negative value, and `formatMs` prints something like `-1:-5:00`. Fix: call `tick()` once when the effect starts running timers, or `setNow(Date.now())` in the `toggleTimer` handler.
- [low] `src/features/cook/wake-lock.ts:18-21`: `acquire` stores the sentinel after `await navigator.wakeLock.request()` without checking that the lock is still wanted. If `release()` or unmount runs while the request is pending, for example Exit right after a tab becomes visible, the new lock is stored with no owner and the screen stays on after leaving cook mode. Two acquires running at once (the visibility handler and `poke`) also overwrite and leak the first sentinel. Fix: after the await, if `!wanted.current || sentinel.current`, release `s` and return.
- [low] `src/features/cook/wake-lock.ts:54-55`: When the 30-minute inactivity timer releases the lock, `wanted` stays true. The `visibilitychange` handler then takes the lock again whenever the user switches back to the tab, with no interaction. That contradicts the "release after 30 min without interaction" rule (SPEC F11). Fix: clear the re-acquire intent in the idle callback, or only re-acquire on visibility when the idle timer has not fired.
- [low] `src/features/cook/CookView.tsx:165`: `useWakeLock()` returns a new object on every render, and `controller`'s `useMemo` depends on `wake`. request changes: one gesture failure path can hang forever, a TTS download has no timeout, and the engine can fire a toggle twice.

- [medium] src/features/gesture/MediaPipeGestureSource.ts:56: if the model fails to load, the catch block runs `const c = await camera;` before it emits `ModelLoadFailed`. SPEC §11.5 notes that an ignored camera permission prompt may never settle. When that happens, the HUD stays on "Starting camera…" forever and never shows the error or the "use the buttons" fallback. Fix: emit the error first, then stop the tracks without waiting, with `void camera.then(c => c.ok && c.s.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()))`.
- [medium] src/features/voice/useVoice.ts:54: the 1.5 s timer stops applying once headers arrive (`clearTimeout` at line 51). After that, `await res.blob()` waits for the whole ElevenLabs stream with no timeout. If the upstream body stalls, `speak()` never resolves. The player stays "speaking" (loading), with no audio and no device-voice fallback, until the user toggles it off. Fix: keep a deadline that also covers `res.blob()`, and fall back to `speechSynthesis` when it expires.
- [medium] src/features/gesture/engine.ts:115: one low-score or misclassified frame while holding a fist or victory sign makes `pose !== this.pose` true. That resets `needRelease` and `fired`, so "must release before re-firing" is defeated. Holding a fist for about 2 s with one jittery frame after the cooldown toggles the timer twice, which pauses a timer the user just started. Fix: only count a pose change after it has lasted a few frames or about `releaseMs`, and add an engine test for this flicker.
- [low] src/features/gesture/MediaPipeGestureSource.ts:69: if the component unmounts while the permission prompt is still open, `stop()` runs before `this.recognizer` is assigned. The cleanup at lines 70-73 only runs after `await camera` settles. If the prompt is never answered, the GestureRecognizer (WASM and GPU resources) is never closed. Fix: check `this.aborted` right after `createRecognizer()` resolves, and close it there.
- [low] src/features/cook/CookView.tsx:257: with auto-read on, `start()` calls `voice.speak(first.text)`. The `restore` dispatch then changes `stepIndex` whenever the resume step or step 0 differs from `session.currentStep`. That triggers the step-change effect at line 170, which calls `stop()` and then `speak()` again. Audio starts, cuts out, and restarts. Fix: drop the `speak` in `start()`, or skip the effect's speak on the first step change after starting.
- [low] src/features/cook/CookView.tsx:98: `prefetch` runs on every step change and at start (line 249) whether or not read-aloud is used. Every cooking session spends paid ElevenLabs characters on steps that are never played, and there is no rate limit yet. Fix: prefetch only when `prefs.autoRead` is on or after read-aloud has been used once.
- [low] src/features/gesture/GestureController.tsx:173: the `role="status"` chip is a polite live region, and its text changes up to 10 times a second ("Ready · 4 s", "Hold fist…", "Scrolling up"). Screen-reader users get a flood of announcements on top of the `say()` live region. Fix: remove `role="status"` and rely on the existing `announce` channel.
- [low] src/features/gesture/GestureController.tsx:112: a fist gesture announces "Timer toggled". The existing effect in CookView also announces "Timer started" or "Timer paused" for the same action, so screen readers hear two announcements. Fix: leave `TIMER_TOGGLE` out of `say(DONE[a])`, as is already done for step changes.
- [low] src/features/cook/CookView.tsx:188: scrolling hardcodes `0.4 * innerHeight`, while `GestureConfig.scrollFraction` (config.ts:7) is defined and never read. The config knob does nothing. Fix: use the config value, or delete the field.

Effort level: medium (reused from last time). Type a level, for example `/code-review high`, to change it.

**Verdict:** request changes. The new point detection skips the confidence checks every other pose has to pass, and it has no hysteresis, so pointing can fire NEXT_STEP/PREV_STEP from noisy frames or fire twice on one long hold.

I couldn't run the vitest suite because the command needed approval, so these findings come from reading the code only.

- [medium] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:119`: `pointDirection(h.landmarks) ?? (low || …)` checks for a point before the `low` (`h.score < minScore`) and `fistMinScore` checks. That means a frame the engine treats as unreliable, which is exactly when the "more_light" hint shows, can still produce `Point_Left`/`Point_Right` and change the step. In a dim kitchen or with a blurred hand, jittery landmarks can pass the geometry test for 800 ms and skip or go back a step. Fix: only call `pointDirection` when the frame isn't low-score (`!low && pointDirection(...)`), and add a test that a low-score point never fires.

- [medium] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:260`: the sideways test `Math.abs(dx) < 2 * Math.abs(dy)` is a hard cutoff with no hysteresis. In this scenario, a user holds the point after NEXT_STEP fires, with the finger near the ~27° limit, so landmark noise drops the pose to `None` for ≥150 ms (`POSE_SETTLE_MS`). The pose change resets `needRelease` and `fired`. When the point comes back, the 1200 ms cooldown and 800 ms hold run again, and a second NEXT_STEP fires during what the user sees as one hold. The test "exactly one NEXT_STEP, even if held" passes only because its landmarks are perfect. Fix: use a looser ratio (e.g. 1.2) once the current pose is already a point, or keep `needRelease` set until the pose is something other than None.

- [low] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:246`: `const ASPECT = 4 / 3` assumes a 640×480 frame. `MediaPipeGestureSource.ts:49` only asks for `ideal` 640×480, so the browser can return 16:9 or a portrait frame on phones. With a portrait 3:4 frame, dx is overstated by about 1.8×, so diagonal and near-vertical points get accepted as sideways. Fix: take the aspect from the video's `videoWidth / videoHeight` and pass it into the engine.

- [low] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:249`: the old swipe check rejected fist-shaped strokes, but the new detector fires on any index-extended, other-fingers-curled hand shape, and per the test (`wins over a misleading classifier label`) the classifier label no longer vetoes it. That shape is the common "index finger on the knife spine" grip while chopping. Held sideways for 800 ms while armed, it changes the step, which is the kind of false trigger SPEC §11 is designed to prevent. Fix: if the classifier says `Closed_Fist` with a high score, let that win over the point, or require the point to stay still.

- [low] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:208`: the HUD reports both point poses as `'Pointing_Up'`. The debug overlay (`GestureController.tsx:188`) therefore shows "Pointing_Up" while the user is pointing sideways. That misleads exactly the threshold tuning SPEC item 14 says is still pending. Fix: show the real point direction in the debug overlay (e.g. a separate debug field).

- [low] `SPEC.md:1623`: the global-cooldown rule still lists "(swipe, timer, speak)", even though the swipe gesture was removed in this change. Fix: change it to "(point, timer, speak)".

- **Chopping:** the finger has to stay still for the hold. An index finger resting on a knife spine keeps moving, so it never fires.

That score is usually high whenever landmarks exist, so the "dim kitchen, blurred hand" guard almost never blocks a point. It can also fall toward 0.5 when the hand is seen edge-on, which is common in a sideways point, so some real points get rejected at random. Fix: gate on a real detection signal, or rely on the landmark geometry and hold-steady checks and drop this gate, and update the code comment to match.

Because `MediaPipeGestureSource` now always sends `handScore`, a dim or blurry hand that the classifier scores low (for example 0.4 on Open_Palm) no longer shows "more light" as long as handedness stays high. The user gets no feedback while gestures silently fail. Fix: use handScore for `lowLight` only when a point is detected, and keep `h.score` for canned poses.

request changes: the new localStorage key wipes every saved cook setting, and the spec still says arming is required even though it is now off by default.

- [medium] `src/features/gesture/settings.ts:12`: changing `KEY` from `"mise.cook-prefs"` to `"mise.cook-prefs.v2"` throws away all saved settings, not just `alwaysArmed`. That includes `showCamera`, `autoRead`, sensitivity, hold time and delegate. Anyone who turned off the camera preview or set the processor to CPU gets the defaults back silently. The old entry also stays in localStorage forever. Fix: keep reading the old key and migrate. If v2 is missing, load `mise.cook-prefs`, delete `gesture.alwaysArmed` so the new default applies, save under v2 and remove the old key.
- [low] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:145`: `anchor` is only cleared when the pose is not in `STILL`. Going straight from `Pointing_Up` to `ILoveYou` (both in `STILL`) keeps the fingertip position from the previous hold. If the tip has moved more than 0.05, the first steady frame sets `poseSince = now`. That drops the 150 ms settle credit, so "previous" takes about 950 ms instead of 800 ms. Fix: clear `anchor` in the pose-change block at lines 125-133, next to `fired = false`.
- [low] `src/features/gesture/engine.ts:141`: the drift check uses normalized x/y with no aspect correction. On a 4:3 camera, 0.05 of width is about 33% more pixels than 0.05 of height, so sideways knife movement is tolerated more than vertical movement. The removed `pointDirection` corrected for this, and this change also deletes `EngineFrame.aspect`. Fix: keep passing `aspect` and scale `dx` by it before `Math.hypot`.
- [low] `SPEC.md:1590`: the gesture table still lists "(prerequisite) Arm … Stirring, chopping and reaching never fire commands". With `alwaysArmed: true` as the default (SPEC.md:1645), that is no longer true: a held `Pointing_Up` or a fist on a spoon fires with no arming step. The chip text at SPEC.md:1670 ("Show your palm to start") is also stale. Fix: mark the Arm row as opt-in when Always armed is off, and update the chip example.

If someone edits that icon (for example to `🖐️`), the "Hold palm: start" hint comes back in always-armed mode with no error. Fix: add a flag to that entry (such as `arm: true`) or filter on the text.
- [low] `src/features/gesture/engine.test.ts:244`: the new tests don't cover two things. One is a direct `Pointing_Up` → `ILoveYou` switch, which is how the stale-anchor bug above would show up. The other is `loadPrefs` handling prefs saved under the old key. Yes, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, but **leave every `AUTH0_*` line blank until you have the real values**. The example's placeholder `AUTH0_DOMAIN=dev-xxxx.us.auth0.com` counts as "set", which switches local auth on and breaks it. With it blank, local dev skips sign-in and uses the demo user.

**Keys and secrets someone has to get**

| Variable | Needed for | Who has it |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET` | Sign-in | Johnny (Auth0 tenant) |
| `AUTH0_SECRET` | Session encryption | Anyone: `openssl rand -hex 32` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Pantry, recipes, cook sessions, meals (all real data) | Johnny (Tiger `mise-db`) |
| `DATABASE_URL_TEST` | `npm run test:db` only | Johnny (Tiger fork `mise-test`) |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Recipe search, label/expiry photos, AI adaptation | Hang |
| `DATAANDAPIS_KEY` | Barcode lookup | Johnny |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | Read-aloud voice (falls back to device voice if missing) | You |

**Fine as they are in the example**
- `APP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000`. Use the real HTTPS domain in production.
- `DB_POOL_MAX`, `GEMINI_MODEL`, `GEMINI_SEARCH_MODEL`, `OFF_BASE_URL`, `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID`, `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID`, `DEFAULT_TZ`.
- `OFF_USER_AGENT` and `RECIPE_FETCH_USER_AGENT` work, but should carry a real contact and domain before the demo.

**Local-only flags**
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_GESTURE_DEBUG=true` shows FPS and the detected pose under the HUD.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_COOK_FIXTURES=true` isn't in the example. Add it so cook mode runs without a database.

what is the database_url_test then

`DATABASE_URL_TEST` points at a **separate, throwaway copy of the database used only by automated tests**. It isn't needed to run or test the app by hand.

- **What it is:** the connection string for a Tiger "fork" of the main database. The spec names it `mise-test`. A fork is an instant copy made with `tiger service fork <service-id> --name mise-test`, so it has the same schema without touching real data.
- **What uses it:** only `npm run test:db`. That command runs the migrations against this database, then runs Hang's database tests: the finish-cooking transaction, "finish twice returns 409", per-user isolation, and the TimescaleDB aggregate. Those tests write and delete rows, which is why they must never run against the real database.
- **What happens without it:** nothing breaks. Plain `npm test`, the dev server and the build all ignore it. The database tests are simply skipped, as they were on `dev`.
- **Who sets it up:** Johnny, as part of creating the Tiger service (johnny.md: "the Tiger service `mise-db` + fork `mise-test`"). It looks like `DATABASE_URL`, just pointing at the fork.

You can leave it blank in `.env.local` until Johnny has the fork. It only matters before merging the cook backend, when someone should run `npm run test:db` once to prove the finish transaction works.

## Installation

- **macOS/Linux/WSL:**
  ```
  curl -fsSL https://cli.tigerdata.com | sh
  ```
- **Windows (PowerShell):**
  ```
  irm https://cli.tigerdata.com/install.ps1 | iex
  ```

Other methods (Homebrew, apt, yum, `go install`) are also listed on the page.

## Authentication

```
tiger auth login
```

The page also documents `--headless`, which lets you authorize with a short code in a browser on any machine.

## tiger service create

The page's only example is:

```
tiger service create --name my-database
```

The page doesn't document the other flags, so run `tiger service create --help` for the full syntax.

## tiger service fork

The page doesn't document this command's syntax. It only lists `fork` as "Fork an existing service." It doesn't cover how to name the fork, which source service to use, or the `--now` and point-in-time options. Run `tiger service fork --help` for those details.

## tiger service list

```
tiger service list
```

The alias `ls` also works (`tiger service ls`).

## tiger db connection-string

The page documents this command as `tiger db uri`, with `connection-string` as an alias:

```
tiger db uri
tiger db connection-string
```

To target a specific service, the page says that anywhere a command takes a service, you can pass either its ID or its exact name as an argument. Its example is `tiger db psql my-api-db`, so the same positional form should apply here, though the page doesn't show it for this command. Names must match exactly, and a name matching more than one service is refused.

The global `--service-id <id>` flag is also available on all commands, and it takes an ID only, not a name:

```
tiger db uri --service-id <id>
```

The `TIGER_SERVICE_ID` environment variable and `tiger config set service_id` can also set a default service, which must be an ID.

You make it by copying the main database with the Tiger CLI, which isn't installed on this machine yet. The copy has to come from the main `mise-db` database, in the same Tiger account as `mise-db`. If Johnny already created `mise-db` in his account, you need access to that account or project first.

Run these in **PowerShell**:

1. **Install the CLI:**
   ```powershell
   irm https://cli.tigerdata.com/install.ps1 | iex
   ```
2. **Log in:**
   ```powershell
   tiger auth login
   ```
3. **Check whether `mise-db` exists:**
   ```powershell
   tiger service list
   ```
   If it's not listed and nobody has made one, create it with `tiger service create --name mise-db`. The free tier allows two databases per account, so `mise-db` plus this test copy uses both.
4. **Make the test copy (a "fork").** I couldn't find this command's exact options in the docs, so check them first:
   ```powershell
   tiger service fork --help
   ```
   Then fork `mise-db` and name the copy `mise-test`.
5. **Get its connection string:**
   ```powershell
   tiger db connection-string mise-test
   ```
6. **Put it in `.env.local`:**
   ```
   DATABASE_URL_TEST=postgres://tsdbadmin:...@host:port/tsdb?sslmode=require
   ```
7. **Run the database tests:**
   ```powershell
   npm run test:db
   ```
   This applies the migrations to the test copy, then runs Hang's database tests (finish-cooking transaction, finishing twice returns 409, per-user isolation, the nutrition aggregate).

Step 7 wouldn't have worked as the code stood: the migration script and the test runner both ignored `.env.local`, so they'd report `DATABASE_URL_TEST` missing even with it set. I fixed both using Node's built-in `.env` loader, with no new dependency. Normal tests still pass (343). The fix is on my local branch with the TTS fix, and neither is pushed.

result.output:
# claude-code review

Effort: medium (reused from last time). Type a level, for example `/code-review high`, to change it.

request changes: the SSRF guard can be bypassed, local dev with auth turned off breaks on every database write, and the search stream has a race and a cancellation leak.

- [medium] `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts:122` and `:153`: the DNS rebinding check is a time-of-check/time-of-use gap. `assertUrlAllowed` resolves the host with `lookup()` and checks the IPs. Then `fetch(url.toString())` resolves the hostname a second time. A domain with a very short TTL can answer a public IP the first time and `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254` the second time. Gemini returns the URLs and the publisher pages can be attacker-controlled, so this reopens the SSRF hole (§13) the module exists to close. Fix: pin the address you checked. Connect through an undici `Agent` with a custom `connect.lookup` that returns only the already-validated address, and keep the Host header and SNI set to the original hostname.

- [medium] `src/lib/current-user.ts:25`: `DEV_USER.id` (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`) is returned whenever `authDisabled` is true, but no migration or seed ever inserts it into `users`. With a real `DATABASE_URL` and no `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, every write that references the user fails its foreign key: `persistOriginal` (recipes.user_id), `createSession`, `setDiscoveryCache`. Every search candidate then shows up as `fetch_failed`, and "Start cooking" returns 500. Fix: in the `authDisabled` branch, run `INSERT INTO users (id, auth0_sub, email, display_name) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` once, for example memoized in a module-level promise.

- [medium] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:116`: `if (stop()) return;` runs before `await persistOriginal(...)`, but `shown++` only runs afterwards, at `:145`. With 5 workers, several can pass the check while `shown` is still below `maxResults`. All of them then persist and emit a candidate. For example, with `maxResults=1`, two workers finish `processExtracted` at the same moment and both stream a candidate, so the client gets more results than it asked for. Fix: reserve the slot synchronously before the await, with `if (shown >= body.maxResults) return; shown++;` (or a separate `reserved` counter), and release it if the persist fails.

- [medium] `src/lib/http.ts:60`: `ndjsonResponse` has no `cancel()` handler and passes no abort signal to `producer`. `SearchStream` aborts the previous search each time the user submits again. On the server, `controller.enqueue` then throws inside the worker's `try`. The `catch` calls `write` again, which throws again. Meanwhile the other workers keep fetching up to 12 publisher pages and running extraction, which may include the Gemini fallback, with nobody reading the results. That wastes rate-limit budget and API cost. Fix: add `cancel() { aborted = true }`, make `write` a no-op once aborted, and expose the `aborted` flag (or an `AbortSignal`) to the producer so the search loop can stop.

- [low] `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts:67`: `isBlockedIp` only matches the literal first hextet `fe80`. Link-local is `fe80::/10`, which covers `fe80` through `febf`, so `fe90::1` and `febf::1` pass. The IPv4 list also leaves out `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT, which holds the metadata service on some clouds), and NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96` isn't decoded. Fix: test `/^fe[89ab]/` on the first hextet, and add `100.64.0.0/10` (plus `198.18.0.0/15` and `224.0.0.0/4`) to the IPv4 checks.

- [low] `src/app/api/tts/route.ts:24`: `checkRateLimit` uses up a token before `Body.safeParse` at `:27`. A client that sends malformed bodies, such as empty text, drains the per-user 60/min budget and gets 429s on valid requests. `recipes/search/route.ts` has the same ordering. Fix: validate the body first, then check the rate limit.

- [low] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:92`: this rebuilds a `PantryItem` from raw rows by hand, about 30 lines. It duplicates `rowToPantryItem` in `src/server/recipes/pantry-view.ts` and loses fields, using `expiryDate: null` and `allergenTags: []`. The two mappings will drift whenever the pantry shape changes. Fix: `SELECT *` and map through `rowToPantryItem(row, tz)`, or call `listPantryByIds`/`listPantryForMatching` with `tx`.

- [low] `src/server/recipes/pantry-view.ts:132`: `getProfileFilters` queries `users` again for diets, allergens and tz right after `requireUser` upserted and returned that same row. That costs every recipes, adapt, search and finish-preview request one extra round trip. Fix: add `diets, allergens` to `requireUser`'s `RETURNING` clause and to `AppUser`, then drop `getProfileFilters`.

- [low] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:68`: `let cached = urls != null;` is followed by `else { cached = true; }` at `:77`, which sets the same value twice. Separately, `mustUse` at `:54` is computed for every request but only read when `mustUsePantryItemIds` is provided. Fix: use `const cached = urls != null;` and compute `mustUse` inside the `if (body.mustUsePantryItemIds)` block.

- [low] `scripts/migrate.mjs:25` and `src/lib/db.ts:20`: `ssl: 'require'` is hard-coded, so `npm run migrate`, `test:db` and the app all fail against a local Postgres or Docker database without TLS, a common setup for teammates. Fix: leave `ssl` unset, since postgres.js honours `?sslmode=require` in the URL, or read it from an env flag.

content.text: Each pinned agent also needs closing after its request, so redirect chains don't leak connections. Wrapping the per-hop code in `try/finally`:

input.command:
python - <<'PYEOF'
p='src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts'
s=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
start=s.index("    const controller = new AbortController();", s.index("const dispatcher = new Agent"))
end_marker="    return { finalUrl: url.toString(), status: res.status, contentType, text };\n"
end=s.index(end_marker,start)+len(end_marker)
body=s[start:end]
body="\n".join(("  "+l if l.strip() else l) for l in body.split("\n"))
new="    try {\n"+body.rstrip()+"\n    } finally {\n      void dispatcher.close().catch(() => {});\n    }\n"
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
PYEOF
